## Row-wise diagonal shear of colored shapes

Observed in task-eac7af5c (three demos; test submission was confirmed correct): for a nonzero object, keep the grid dimensions and color, and shear each colored cell horizontally according to its row. Let `r_bottom` be the bottommost row containing the object. Map each colored cell `(r, c)` to `(r, c + r - r_bottom)`, equivalently shift row `r` left by `r_bottom - r` columns. Leave all other cells zero; discard any mapped cells outside the grid. This leaves the bottom row unchanged and shifts each successively higher row farther left.

Verified demo examples: a 5-row object shifts its top row left by 4 columns; a 3-row object shifts its top row left by 2; the six-row test object shifts its top row left by 6. The transformation applies cellwise, preserving gaps and overlaps as mapped pixels (not as a bounding-box redraw).
